high.title: This Brazilian Stock Can Benefit Even from a 'Worst Possible Scenario' for Selic Rate, According to Analyst; Find Out Why
high.summary: Brazil's Selic rate cutting cycle, widely expected for 2026, began at the last COPOM meeting on March 18th. However, the magnitude of cuts may not meet initial market expectations. By mid-February, most of the market was pricing in a terminal Selic rate of 12% annually for 2026. Now, with the Middle East war bringing greater inflationary pressure, expectations have deteriorated significantly. According to Ruy Hungria, analyst at Empiricus Research, "If we started the year with a perspective of seeing Selic at 12% at the end of 2026, now this number has already been revised to 13.5%-13.75%, and could rise further depending on the extension of the conflict." This shift represents a dramatic repricing of Brazil's monetary policy outlook, with the terminal rate now expected 150-175 basis points higher than initially forecast. For BRL traders, this suggests a more hawkish BCB stance that could support the Real against USD, while bond investors should prepare for higher yields across the curve. The geopolitical risk premium is now firmly embedded in Brazilian rate expectations.

high.summary: The Ibovespa is tracking a battery of Chinese economic data including GDP, industrial production, retail sales, and unemployment rate, while Brazil releases retail sales numbers and IGP-10 inflation data. President Trump indicated that the war against Iran is "very close to the end" with Tehran showing willingness for an agreement, which could impact commodity prices and risk sentiment affecting Brazilian equities.

medium.title: Oil Rises Despite Expectations of Resumed US-Iran Negotiations
medium.summary: Brent crude futures rose 0.90% to $95.64/barrel while WTI gained 0.46% to $91.70, despite expectations of resumed US-Iran peace negotiations. The war has virtually shut down traffic through the Strait of Hormuz, crucial for global oil transport. President Trump suggested negotiations with Tehran could resume this week, which would impact global energy markets and potentially affect Petrobras and Brazil's energy sector positioning.
